Akpabio, in a condolence statement issued by his Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Anietie Ekong, on Wednesday in Abuja, described Edochie as an accomplished actor and cultural ambassador whose exceptional talent and appreciation of African traditions earned him admiration across generations.
He said the veteran actor, through decades of dedication to his craft, brought Nigerian stories, values and traditions to life, contributing immensely to the growth and international recognition of Nollywood.
According to him, Edochie’s memorable performances and distinctive delivery made him a household name and an enduring symbol of excellence in Nigeria’s creative industry.
The Senate President further acknowledged the actor’s immense contributions to the preservation and promotion of Nigerian and African heritage, noting that his legacy would continue to inspire upcoming actors and generations of creative practitioners.
“Chief Pete Edochie was a towering figure in Nigeria’s entertainment industry. His talent, wisdom, discipline and commitment to his craft distinguished him as one of the finest actors of his generation.
“He used his platform to project our culture and identity to the world. His contributions will not be forgotten,” Akpabio said.
He extended his heartfelt condolences to the Edochie family, the government and people of Anambra State, the Actors Guild of Nigeria and the entire Nollywood community.
Akpabio prayed that God would grant the deceased’s family, friends, colleagues and admirers the fortitude to bear the loss, while granting the departed eternal rest.
